digest.en: Abelardo De La Espriella dominates headlines as Colombia's new President. Trump's threat to Iran is also a major story. Iran walked out of talks after the threat.
digest.hi: मध्य पूर्व और अफ्रीका में ईरान-अमेरिका की वार्ता सफल रही। दोनों देशों के प्रतिनिधिमंडल ने आंतरिक परामर्श करने का फैसला किया। वार्ता के बाद कुवैत एयरपोर्ट में ड्रोन हमले के बाद आग लग गई।

articles.title: Who is Abelardo De La Espriella, Colombia's new right-wing President?
articles.summary: Abelardo De La Espriella, known as "The Tiger," is Colombia's new right-wing president. He campaigned on an anti-establishment platform promising economic revival and order against illegal armed groups and drug trafficking. Nicknamed “The Tiger” by his followers, Mr. De La Espriella portrayed himself as an anti-establishment savior capable of reviving Colombia’s ailing economy and restoring order in a country rattled by illegal armed groups and drug trafficking.

articles.title: Jack Neo announces open casting call for new Ah Boys To Firemen film
articles.summary: Jack Neo's J Team Productions announced an open casting call for its new film "Ah Boys To Firemen." The production company is seeking male and female actors of all races, aged in their twenties and thirties. A post on the social media pages of the Jack Neo-founded J Team Productions revealed that the film production company was looking for female and male talents, of all races, in their twenties and thirties for the upcoming movie.

articles.title: Prada rethinks luxury menswear with a jeans-inspired spring 2027 collection
articles.summary: Prada presented a spring 2027 menswear collection inspired by jeans. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons reimagined classic five-pocket trousers and cropped jackets using leather and technical fabrics for a universal approach. At Milan Fashion Week, Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons turned to the simplicity of five-pocket trousers and cropped jackets, reimagining everyday staples in leather and technical fabrics while arguing for a more universal approach to fashion.

articles.title: Iranians walk out of talks venue after Trump threat
articles.summary: Iranian negotiators departed the Geneva venue after President Trump threatened sanctions. The talks aimed to resolve decades-old U. S.-Iranian disputes. A 60-day period was intended for broader issue settlement. The negotiations to end a war that sowed chaos across the region and rattled the global economy are meant to trigger a 60-day period to settle broader issues that have dogged U. S.-Iranian relations for decades.

articles.title: Taliban Smashes Smartphones As Restrictions Deepen In Afghanistan
articles.summary: The Taliban has started restricting smartphone use among government employees in Afghanistan. Enforcement is uneven across the country. The Taliban has begun restricting the use of smartphones by government employees, although the order appears to be unevenly enforced across the country. In some areas, civilians' mobile devices have reportedly been targeted as well, sparking concern that the ban may eventually extend nationwide.

articles.title: Trump Threatens To Hit Iran 'Very Hard' Over Hezbollah 'Proxies'
articles.summary: Delegations from the United States, Iran, Qatar, and Pakistan gathered on June Delegations from the United States, Iran, Qatar and Pakistan began gathering on June 21 at the Lake Lucerne Summit, launching what could become the most consequential diplomatic effort yet to stabilize the Middle East after weeks of war. Delegations Gather For US-Iran Summit Amid Fragile Regional Truce. High-level talks have begun between US Vice President JD Vance and Iranian representatives at the Burgenstock resort in Switzerland, launching what could become the most consequential diplomatic effort yet to stabilize the Middle East after near four months of war.

articles.title: Sweat, tears and camaraderie as 20,000 runners take on world’s largest ultramarathon
articles.summary: Twenty thousand runners competed in the Comrades race in South Africa. For one day every June, South Africa’s searing racial inequality seems to melt away at Comrades raceIn the early morning dark, thousands of runners waited, jostling with anticipation. South Africa’s national anthem rang out. Then the haunting swell of Shosholoza, first sung by Zimbabwean migrant workers in South Africa’s goldmines.

articles.title: What's In A Name? Tajikistan Tightens Rules On What Children Can Be Called
articles.summary: Tajikistan officials rejected a couple's chosen name for their newborn. A Tajik couple was forced to abandon the name they chose for their newborn child after officials said it was not on an approved registry. The case highlights Tajikistan's controversial effort to promote Persian-rooted names and curb visible Islamic influences. What's In A Name? Tajikistan Tightens Rules On What Children Can Be Called.

articles.title: Canada’s policies force asylum seekers into US to face deportation, critics say
articles.summary: Advocates state Canada's Safe Third Country Agreement compels asylum seekers to enter the Advocates say the Safe Third Country Agreement forces immigrants to head to an unsafe country: the United StatesIt was the threat of gang violence in Honduras that pushed Carlos and Antonia to flee their home. In 2021, with their toddler, Alejandro, and a handful of belongings, the married couple ventured north hoping to reach safety in the US. The journey, through Guatemala and Mexico, was filled.

articles.title: What Indonesia’s finance chief really brought back from Beijing
articles.summary: Indonesia’s Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa secured Chinese backing for Indonesia When Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa landed in Beijing last week, the official agenda appeared straightforward: secure support for Indonesia’s first sovereign Panda Bond, deepen financial cooperation with China and strengthen investor confidence. By those measures, the visit was productive. Purbaya returned with Chinese backing for the Panda Bond initiative, discussions on expanding yuan-rup.

articles.title: Ghost of far-right paramilitaries hovers over Colombia’s presidential runoff vote
articles.summary: Colombia holds a presidential runoff vote on Sunday. Colombians will choose on Sunday between two men whose lives have been very differently shaped by the militias, and whose visions for the country are poles apartWhoever wins Sunday’s presidential runoff vote in Colombia, the country’s next leader will have a personal history intertwined with one of the criminal forces at the heart of a decades-long armed conflict that claimed nearly half a million.

articles.title: For One 21-Year-Old New Zealander, War In Ukraine Means A Chance To 'Fight For Freedom'
articles.summary: A 21-year-old New Zealander, known by his call A soldier who goes by the call sign Kiwi was still a teenager in Wellington, New Zealand, when he saw Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on the news in February 2022. As the war dragged on, he learned that he could enlist and receive training to fight alongside the forces defending Ukraine.

articles.title: Everything Bangladesh’s Rahman hopes to get from China
articles.summary: Bangladesh Investment Development Authority chairman Ashik Chowdhury stated defense issues would be discussed during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s upcoming trip When Ashik Chowdhury, the executive chairman of the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority, was recently asked about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s upcoming trip to China, his response caught the room off guard. “Many issues will come up,” Chowdhury remarked, “starting with defense.” For a diplomatic trip strictly billed around trade, investment, and business, it was an [] The post Everythi.

articles.title: A Precarious Mountain Pass Is Bringing New Life To A Kyrgyz Village
articles.summary: Zardaly, a Kyrgyz village in the Batken region, is seeing its only access road expanded and reinforced. Previously, the precarious mountain pass was dangerous for people and horses, with some falling to their deaths. The infrastructure improvements are bringing new life to the area. New housing is being built. A power station is also planned for Zardaly. In Kyrgyzstan's remote Batken region, locals say people and horses have fallen to their deaths while traversing the only road to the village of Zardaly.

articles.title: Iranian Artist, Activist, And Filmmaker Marjane Satrapi Honored At Paris Memorial
articles.summary: Marjane Satrapi was laid to rest in Paris on June 19. The Iranian-born author wrote the graphic novel Persepolis, which was later adapted into a Cannes-winning animated film. Satrapi's work was honored with tributes in Paris. She was a renowned artist, activist, and filmmaker. Iranian-born author Marjane Satrapi, who wrote the hit graphic novel Persepolis, was laid to rest on June 19 in Paris amid tributes honoring her work.

articles.title: Gas Shortages Hit Russia As Ukraine Hits Refineries
articles.summary: Russia is experiencing gas shortages at fuel stations. Pulling up at a gas station with no fuel for sale, a Russian woman is aghast: “What’s going on in this country?” What’s going on is that in the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, Ukraine is fighting back with strikes on oil refineries, part of a bid to bring the war to citizens across Russia.

articles.title: US-Iran talks delayed as Israeli bombs in Lebanon kill 18 or more
articles.summary: US and Iranian delegations delayed travel to Switzerland for peace talks after Israeli military bombardment in southern Lebanon US and Iranian delegations delayed plans to travel to Switzerland on Friday for the opening round of talks to cement the details of a peace agreement as the Israeli military bombarded southern Lebanon, killing at least 18 people and threatening once again to derail momentum toward a diplomatic resolution.

articles.title: Art and culture can both fuel and counter hate, UN discussion hears on Juneteenth
articles.summary: Artists at the United Nations used cultural artifacts and performances to illustrate how art can counter hate. Examples included an enslaved African's gold collar and Holocaust-era music. A staged hate radio broadcast and participatory porcelain cup displays were also presented. From a gold collar worn by an enslaved African to music preserved for nearly a century after the Holocaust, a staged reconstruction of a hate radio broadcast or porcelain coffee cups laid out in participatory remembrance, artists in a United Nations discussion on Friday used powerful images to underscore how culture can shape the fight against hatred.

articles.title: Wasian and proud . but does the label uplift or divide?
articles.summary: The term "Wasian" is gaining visibility in popular culture. “Wasians” are having a moment right now. Think of Winter Olympians Alysa Liu and Eileen Gu, singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo, actors Lola Tang (The Summer I Turned Pretty) and Hudson Williams (Heated Rivalry), or singer/dancer Megan Skiendiel from Katseye. In fact, Icelandic-Chinese singer Laufey featured many of these same “Wasians” in her recent Madwoman music video.

articles.title: Severe thunderstorms sweep Europe and east Asia
articles.summary: Severe thunderstorms caused destruction in the Balkans last week. The storms formed over the Adriatic Sea due to lingering hot air and a southward cold front. Slovenia experienced strong winds and heavy rain. Strong winds and heavy rain batter Slovenia, while France experiences atypical heatwaveSevere thunderstorms swept across the Balkans last week, bringing widespread destruction to parts of the region.

articles.title: India doubts drove Pentagon’s Indo-Pacific name change
articles.summary: The Pentagon restored the US Pacific Command designation, replacing Indo-Pacific Command. The Department of Defense stated this is a historical adjustment, with the area of responsibility unchanged from America's coast to India's border. The Pentagon’s decision to restore the designation US Pacific Command (USPACOM), replacing the Indo-Pacific Command name adopted in 2018, has officially been presented as a historical adjustment rather than a strategic shift.

articles.title: Barbados prime minister announces manifesto for slavery reparations
articles.summary: Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley announced a new manifesto for slavery reparations. The document, which highlights harm to African women, asserts the moral, ethical, and legal case for reparations from Caribbean leaders. Updated document, which emphasises harm done to African women, is being considered by other Caribbean countriesBarbados’s prime minister, Mia Mottley, has announced a new manifesto from Caribbean leaders asserting the “moral, ethical and legal case” for reparations over damage caused by hundreds of years of enslavement. articles.title: Repair Crews Start Emergency Work To Save War-Damaged Kyiv Cathedral
articles.summary: Ukrainian workers began emergency repairs on a historic Kyiv Cathedral, part of a UNESCO-protected Ukrainian workers are conducting emergency repairs to a historic cathedral, part of a UNESCO-protected monastery, which was damaged in an overnight attack on June 15. While priceless items were moved to safety, experts warn that soot and moisture continue to threaten other historic artifacts. Repair Crews Start Emergency Work To Save War-Damaged Kyiv Cathedral.

articles.summary: South African courts sentenced Dawie Groenewald and Tielman Erasmus ‘Mastermind’ Dawie Groenewald given fine of 2m rand or four-year jail term almost 16 years after arrestTwo traffickers of rhino horns have been sentenced by a South African court in what police said was the world’s largest such case, partly bringing to an end an almost two-decade legal saga. articles.summary: Max Mara celebrated its 75th anniversary with a catwalk show in Shanghai. The event paid tribute to Chinese style, reflecting the city's dynamic energy. Designer Ian Griffiths noted Shanghai's constant motion as a key reason for choosing the location. The brand aims to connect with China's luxury consumers.
